how: Stitched with ffmpeg from the finished, already-aired shorts (no re-render, no new narration, no new facts). Each short is cut just before its 'Comment your town' ending; only the last one keeps it. Kingsford Heights is the Nov. 16 remake (its .srt in out/ is still the old cut, so the cut point, 49.08 s, was found from the frames).
youtube_title: LaPorte County After Dark: 8 stories from the county's dark history
youtube:
Eight stories from LaPorte County's dark history, back to back: a headless figure by the tracks near Stillwell, a newspaper hoax in Wanatah, a lighthouse family lost on Lake Michigan, the war plant at Kingsbury and the town built beside it, the 1965 Palm Sunday tornado, the picnic boat that never reached Michigan City, and a handcar on the tracks near Fish Lake. Legends are told as legends.

0:00 Stillwell: the headless figure at Flaherty station
0:45 Wanatah: the petrified woman, an 1891 newspaper hoax
1:24 Michigan City: the keeper's son and the pier light, 1878
2:12 Kingsbury: the farms that became a war plant, 1940
2:53 Kingsford Heights: the empty wartime town, 1942
3:42 Wanatah: the Palm Sunday tornado, 1965
4:29 Michigan City: the Eastland, 1915
5:14 Fish Lake: the handcar and Swift's ice houses, 1897

Comment your town, and it could be next!
#LaPorteAfterDark #LaPorte #LaPorteCounty #Indiana #History

All pictures are drawn. Narration is a computer voice. Every story here first ran as its own LaPorte After Dark short.
Sources:
Stillwell: La Porte County Historical Society Museum (La Porte Weekly Herald, Nov. 19, 1903); Indianapolis Journal, Nov. 15, 1903, and 1905 reprints, via Tim Prasil, Brom Bones Books, and Strange Ago.
Wanatah petrified woman: Wanatah Historical Society (from the Valparaiso Star, May 29, 1891); Indiana's Lincoln Highway Byway guide; 1891 reprints via DigitalNC.
Michigan City pier light: National Park Service, Sleeping Bear Dunes; Lighthousefriends; Lighthouse Digest; U.S. Coast Guard History; Old Lighthouse Museum, Michigan City.
Kingsbury: WKVI archives; Indiana Public Media, Moment of Indiana History; The History Museum, South Bend; Indiana DNR; Indiana Landmarks.
Kingsford Heights: Town of Kingsford Heights; Towne Post (2022); "New Deal Ghost Town," Garfield County News (Panguitch, Utah), Sept. 28, 1944; ProPublica, "Bombs in Your Backyard" (Defense Department cleanup data, 2015); Indiana DNR, Kingsbury Fish & Wildlife Area maps.
Wanatah tornado: National Weather Service (Northern Indiana, Chicago, Indianapolis); Storm Prediction Center history; The Times of Northwest Indiana (2015).
Eastland: National Archives at Chicago; Encyclopaedia Britannica; WTTW; Michigan City Historical Society; Associated Press.
Fish Lake: The Westchester Tribune (Chesterton), Oct. 16, 1897, via Porter County INGenWeb; The Portable LaPorte County (c. 1978, Michigan City Public Library).
More LaPorte County history: https://laporteweathernow.com/history
